package_info.package_versions: Windows and MacOS builds affected in March-April 2023
package_info.why_malicious: The 3CXDesktopApp was compromised in a supply chain attack, resulting in the delivery of multiple malware payloads (TAXHAUL/TxRLoader, COLDCAT, SIMPLESEA) that enabled code execution, persistence, and remote command-and-control, all without user consent.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: TAXHAUL (TxRLoader) decrypts and executes shellcode from <machine hardware profile GUID>.TxR.0.regtrans-ms
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the loader decrypts and executes shellcode embedded in a file within the Windows TxR directory, resulting in the in-memory execution of a downloader (COLDCAT) that can fetch further payloads.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Legitimate applications do not decrypt and execute arbitrary shellcode from obscure system directories.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal software should not execute code from files in the TxR directory, nor should it decrypt and run shellcode at runtime.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some security tools or updaters may use encrypted payloads for self-updating, but not from system TxR directories.
key_indicators: Decryption and execution of shellcode from a non-standard file location
Use of system directories to hide payloads
In-memory execution to evade disk-based detection

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: COLDCAT downloader (shellcode) connects to C2 domains (e.g., azureonlinecloud[.]com, akamaicontainer[.]com, journalide[.]org, msboxonline[.]com) to fetch additional payloads.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After being loaded in-memory, the shellcode establishes outbound network connections to attacker-controlled C2 domains to download and execute further malicious payloads.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unexpected outbound connections to suspicious domains from a desktop application are highly anomalous.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate desktop apps should not connect to unknown C2 infrastructure or download and execute arbitrary code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Auto-updaters may contact update servers, but not unlisted or suspicious domains.
key_indicators: Outbound connections to known C2 domains

execution_context.trigger: runtime (on MacOS, post-installation or application launch)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: SIMPLESEA MacOS backdoor located at /Library/Graphics/Quartz (MD5: d9d19abffc2c7dac11a16745f4aea44f)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the backdoor executes on MacOS, providing remote access and command execution capabilities to the attacker, likely communicating with C2 infrastructure.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: A binary masquerading as a graphics library in a non-standard location is highly suspicious, especially with a known malicious hash.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate applications should not drop or execute unauthorized binaries in /Library/Graphics/Quartz.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; this is not a standard location for legitimate binaries.

execution_context.file_location: DLL loaded via side-loading in the context of legitimate Microsoft Windows binaries

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious DLL side-loaded by legitimate Windows binaries to execute TAXHAUL malware.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At application launch, a malicious DLL is loaded by a trusted Windows binary, resulting in the execution of attacker code (TAXHAUL) with the privileges of the legitimate process.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: DLL side-loading is a well-known technique for evading detection and achieving persistence.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate applications should not load unauthorized DLLs, especially those that execute malware.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate software may use DLL injection for debugging, but not for executing malware.
key_indicators: Execution of malware in the context of legitimate processes

attack_chain.action: Malicious DLL is side-loaded by a legitimate Windows binary, executing TAXHAUL (TxRLoader) malware.
attack_chain.leads_to: Decryption and execution of shellcode from TxR directory

attack_chain.action: TAXHAUL decrypts and executes shellcode from <machine hardware profile GUID>.TxR.0.regtrans-ms.
COLDCAT downloader establishes outbound connections to C2 domains and fetches additional payloads.
On MacOS, SIMPLESEA backdoor is installed and provides remote access to attackers.
attack_chain.leads_to: Persistence and remote control on MacOS systems

behavioral_signatures: DLL side-loading by legitimate Windows binaries
Decryption and execution of shellcode from files in C:\Windows\System32\config\TxR\
Outbound network connections to suspicious C2 domains
Presence of unauthorized binaries in /Library/Graphics/Quartz on MacOS
file_indicators: Unexpected DLLs loaded by trusted Windows binaries
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for DLL side-loading activity by legitimate Windows binaries, especially those loading unauthorized DLLs. Detect decryption and execution of shellcode from files in the TxR directory. Alert on outbound connections to known C2 domains. On MacOS, flag the presence of binaries in /Library/Graphics/Quartz, especially with known malicious hashes. Correlate these behaviors for high-confidence detection of this supply chain attack.
